fields.peterl\n\n 2013-06-04 08:36\n\ndeveloper:
TopSurnames uses a different algorithm than Statistics and SurnameCloud, which uses identical algorithm.

The difference occurs when you have both primary and alternate surnames.

Do you have many alternate surnames?
fields.jduemes\n\n 2013-06-04 09:00\n\nreporter:
I would say yes.

If a woman, i.e. "Paula Souza" marries with "Roberto Varela" and she gives up her birth name Souza having only Paula Varela after marriage, I add a Alternative name as Married Name for her. This is very convenient to keep the information.

Did I understand your question correctly ? Is this what you mean with "alternate surnames" ?
fields.peterl\n\n 2013-06-04 12:22\n\ndeveloper:
Yes. However, I don't think that alternate name was intended to be used for "Married Name". There was a discussion recently in the Gramps UsersList about this. See:

https://sourceforge.net/p/gramps/mailman/message/30922244/

I have used alternate name only when a person changed its surname (not by marriage).

fields.vassilii\n\n 2013-06-11 21:48\n\ndevelop:
First, it sounds that, no matter what, the two gramplets should have the same logic wrt what is counted and what is not, best if it's done using the same common code.

The easiest thing would probably be to change both gramplets to report "total unique primary surnames".

Another option would be to count each and every surname, but then you also have to consider special cases like patronymic/patronymic-without-actual-surname etc.

FWIW, In my database, I use alias for two scenarios:
1) Alternative spelling in a different source, most notably, Russian official name vs original Jewish rabbinical record. This sometimes can be as different, e.g., "Michael" vs "Moshe".

2) Like you, when the person underwent a name change not through a marriage event.
fields.peterl\n\n 2013-06-12 14:58\n\ndeveloper:
The gramplets "SurnameCloudGramplet" and "StatsGramplet" use the same algorithm.

"TopSurnameGramplet" uses another algorithm.

Tested with my tree.

"TopSurnameGramplet" counts empty surnames. This has been fixed.

"af Ekenstam" in SurnameCloudGramplet/StatsGramplet
is counted as "Ekenstam" in Stats, which is OK.

"Ersson Wänman" in SurnameCloudGramplet/StatsGramplet is not counted in Stats.
Both "Ersson" and "Wänman" are counted in all three.
Ersson is a patronymicon, Wänman is a "taken name"

"Olofsson Landgren" in SurnameCloudGramplet/StatsGramplet is not counted in Stats.
Both "Olofsson" and "Landgren" are counted in all three.
Olofsson is name by birth and Landgren is new alias.
Using alternate nam.

SurnameCloudGramplet gives 1209 names
StatsGramplet gives 1209
TopSurnameGramplet gives 1207, which is correct as the names
"Ersson Wänman" and "Olofsson Landgren" are not counted in TopSurnameGramplet.

The correct number is 1209.
